open_risks.risk: Reviewers may dismiss the benchmark as wall-hit detection if T1/T5 dominate the paper narrative.
open_risks.mitigation: Lead with the T1/T2/T4 triad and present T3/T5 as coverage extensions.

open_risks.risk: Hidden or off-image geometry can silently determine labels, especially for T3 and T5.
open_risks.mitigation: Require visible_sweep_ratio >= 0.7, fov_supported=true, requires_hidden_geometry=false, and collision_point_visible when applicable.

open_risks.risk: Shortcut baselines may solve many cases without swept-volume reasoning.
open_risks.mitigation: Run blind, majority, radius-only, action-only, center-ray, largest-floor-patch, and corridor-width heuristics before any claim.

open_risks.risk: T4 can be gamed by monotonic body-size priors if options always expose the smaller body.
open_risks.mitigation: Randomize body order, include both-complete and neither-complete no-flip controls, and report pair consistency.

open_risks.risk: Simulator artifacts can create noisy labels around glass, thin structures, depth holes, overhangs, and movable objects.
open_risks.mitigation: Discard ambiguous cases and require RGB, depth, top-down, sweep overlay, oracle trace, and ambiguity_reason for audit.

open_risks.risk: Body-width normalization helps but does not fully remove monocular scale ambiguity.
open_risks.mitigation: Keep fixed camera height in the demo and include human sanity, M2b sweep overlay, and M3 depth probes.

open_risks.risk: The answers below are illustrative and may be wrong for any real RGB frame until oracle metadata is attached.
open_risks.mitigation: Replace or verify every label from data_manifest.json before public release or model scoring.

open_risks.risk: T3 and T5 can require hidden or off-image geometry if sampled carelessly.
open_risks.mitigation: Keep only cases with fov_supported=true, visible_sweep_ratio>=0.7, and requires_hidden_geometry=false.

open_risks.risk: T4 can be solved by monotonic body-size shortcuts if body order is fixed.
open_risks.mitigation: Randomize Body A/Body B order, include both/no-flip/neither controls, and score counterfactual pair consistency.

open_risks.risk: Prompt wording can leak answers if it describes gaps, obstacles, or passability.
open_risks.mitigation: Questions below state only body, action, and options; geometric explanation is confined to rationale.

open_risks.risk: Unpublishable benchmark if labels or examples remain template-authored rather than deterministic simulator outputs.
open_risks.mitigation: Block public claims until every case is generated from the swept-cylinder oracle with non-null visibility metadata and audit visualizations.

open_risks.risk: False novelty if the benchmark is solved by language priors or simple 2D heuristics.
open_risks.mitigation: Require blind, majority, radius-only, action-only, center-ray, corridor-width, and largest-floor-patch baselines before claiming embodied reasoning.

open_risks.risk: Hidden-geometry leakage, especially for T3 turn-then-forward and T5 fixed passability.
open_risks.mitigation: Keep T3/T5 extension-only unless fov_supported=true, visible_sweep_ratio>=0.7, requires_hidden_geometry=false, and decisive collision evidence is visible.

open_risks.risk: T4 can be gamed by monotonic body-size reasoning because the smaller body is usually the successful option.
open_risks.mitigation: Randomize body order, include both/neither controls, score pair consistency, and require same-image flip_pair_id evidence.

open_risks.risk: Body-width normalization may still be too hard from monocular RGB without calibrated camera/height cues.
open_risks.mitigation: Run human sanity checks and M2b/M3 probes to separate visual scale limits from swept-volume reasoning failures.

open_risks.risk: Taxonomy may look borrowed from spatial-intelligence benchmarks if presented too broadly.
open_risks.mitigation: Use EgoConseq-specific readouts: forward extent, directional sweep comparison, action-sequence consequence, body intervention, visible passability.

open_risks.risk: Unvalidated text templates could be mistaken for benchmark cases in the HTML deliverables.
open_risks.mitigation: Block ready_for_showcase_review; require simulator-backed data_manifest fields and per-case review before any case is shown.

open_risks.risk: A live --runner codex HTML/design round would polish placeholders instead of producing evidence.
open_risks.mitigation: Route the next phase to pipeline_verify/case generation, producing data_manifest.json and visualization assets before HTML case pages.

open_risks.risk: T3 and T5 can leak hidden geometry or collapse into shortcut tasks.
open_risks.mitigation: Keep them extension-only and require fov_supported=true, visible_sweep_ratio>=0.7, requires_hidden_geometry=false, and shortcut baseline checks.

open_risks.risk: T4 can be solved by monotonic body-size priors if body order and answer distribution are fixed.
open_risks.mitigation: Randomize body order, include flip and no-flip groups, and score pair consistency by counterfactual_group_id.

open_risks.risk: False novelty if the benchmark is described as new collision geometry or broad spatial intelligence.
open_risks.mitigation: State that swept-cylinder collision is the label engine; novelty is single-frame ego-body action-consequence diagnosis.

motivation: EgoConseq-Bench evaluates whether a vision-language model can infer the visible local physical consequence of its own body executing a short action from one egocentric RGB image. It is not navigation, generic spatial relations, object physics, or hidden-space inference; it isolates body-conditioned ego swept-volume consequence reasoning.

adjudication.rationale: The showcase needs 10 reviewed-surviving cases for each core task before HTML review.

design_principles: Single-image ego-action VQA: one RGB frame, one body description, one action primitive, one answer.
Body is a query-conditioned causal collision operator: do(body=r) can flip the consequence on the same image and action.
Distances are normalized by body width, with 1 body-width = 2r, avoiding absolute monocular metric claims.
Labels come from deterministic swept-cylinder geometry and visibility filtering, not LLM judgment.
Core cases must be visible or directly inferable from the current egocentric RGB/depth render: no hidden-corner, off-image, or occluded decisive geometry.
Counterfactual body/action pairs, blind controls, option balancing, and shortcut heuristics are mandatory validity checks.
Swept-cylinder collision is the label engine, not the novelty claim; novelty is the isolated diagnostic of MLLM embodied consequence grounding.

spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.name: Body-width forward swept extent
inspired_by: Prior spatial benchmarks only as motivation-to-QA design examples
spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.goal_fit: Reads how far the queried cylindrical body can move forward before first visible collision, normalized by body width.

spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.name: Visible directional swept-volume comparison
inspired_by: VSI-Bench / Thinking in Space only as methodology inspiration
spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.goal_fit: Compares candidate visible sweeps in small egocentric angles without relying on route planning or hidden space.

spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.name: Short composite ego-action consequence
inspired_by: MindCube only as what-if QA construction inspiration, not hidden-space reasoning
spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.goal_fit: Compares a small turn-then-forward consequence with straight motion under the same visible-local swept-volume boundary.

spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.name: Body-intervention consequence
inspired_by: Counterfactual QA methodology only; the intervention is EgoConseq's do(body=r) collision operator
spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.goal_fit: Holds image and action fixed while changing radius to test embodiment-sensitive consequence flips and no-flip controls.

spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.name: Visible fixed-horizon passability
inspired_by: Prior benchmarks only as coverage-design precedent
spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.goal_fit: Asks whether a visible forward swept corridor is contact-free for the queried body, without semantic object-physics claims.

tasks.question_template: Body: cylinder radius {r} m, height 1.5 m. Action: move straight forward. How many body-widths can it move before first contact? Options: <2, 2-4, 4-8, >8.
tasks.answer_derivation: Compute forward max_safe_distance_body_widths on the radius-specific navmesh and bin into <2 / 2-4 / 4-8 / >8; require visible_sweep_ratio>=0.7, fov_supported=true, requires_hidden_geometry=false, collision_point_visible when applicable, and bin_margin_body_widths>=0.5.

tasks.question_template: Body: cylinder radius {r} m, height 1.5 m. Candidate directions: left-front {theta} degrees, straight, right-front {theta} degrees. Rank them by maximum distance before first contact, longest to shortest.
tasks.answer_derivation: Compute swept distances for {-theta,0,+theta}, sort descending, require all candidates FOV-supported, and discard near-tie rankings unless ranking_margin_body_widths is sufficient. theta defaults to 30 degrees with 15 degrees allowed.

tasks.question_template: Same RGB and action: move straight forward for {horizon} body-widths, where each body-width equals that body's diameter. Body A radius {r_a} m and Body B radius {r_b} m, height 1.5 m. Which bodies complete the action without contact? Options: both bodies, only Body A, only Body B, neither body.
tasks.answer_derivation: At the same pose/action/horizon, compare passability across radius-specific navmeshes; randomize body order; generate flip and no-flip controls with counterfactual_group_id and flip_pair_id; report pair consistency.

tasks.question_template: Body: cylinder radius {r} m, height 1.5 m. Compare A) move straight forward and B) rotate {theta} degrees, then move forward. Which action allows more body-widths before first contact? Options: A, B, about the same.
tasks.answer_derivation: Compare straight max distance with turn-then-forward max distance; label about the same only within tie_margin_body_widths=0.5. Extension-only until FOV support, hidden-geometry filters, and shortcut checks pass.

tasks.question_template: Body: cylinder radius {r} m, height 1.5 m. Action: move forward for {horizon} body-widths within the currently visible region. Is the swept body contact-free? Options: yes, no.
tasks.answer_derivation: Check whether every swept sample through the fixed horizon remains navigable for the radius-specific body. Extension-only until hidden-geometry filters and radius-only/centerline shortcut checks pass.

qa_design.name: Body-Width Forward Horizon
qa_design.question_pattern: Ask how many body widths the queried cylindrical body can move straight forward before first visible contact.

qa_design.name: Visible Directional Sweep Ranking
qa_design.question_pattern: Rank left-front, straight, and right-front swept distances within the current FOV.

qa_design.name: Composite Motion Consequence
qa_design.question_pattern: Compare straight motion with a small turn-then-forward action under the same body constraints.

qa_design.name: Body Counterfactual Sweep
qa_design.question_pattern: Hold RGB and action fixed while changing body radius, then ask which bodies complete the sweep.
qa_design.answer_space: both / only Body A / only Body B / neither

qa_design.name: Visible Passability
qa_design.question_pattern: Ask whether a fixed forward swept horizon in the visible region is contact-free for the queried body.

novelty_positioning: EgoConseq is single-frame, ego-body, action-conditioned consequence VQA; it is not route navigation, active exploration, or long-horizon planning.
The benchmark does not claim novel collision geometry; swept-cylinder intersection is the deterministic label engine.
Compared with PhysBench, it asks about the ego body rather than object or scene physics.
Compared with CapNav, it is one-step visible-local consequence reasoning rather than route-level capability-conditioned navigation.
Compared with TouchSafeBench, it uses a hypothetical action from single RGB rather than multi-view/current collision grounding.
Compared with ENACT and EXPLORE-Bench, it isolates body-width swept-volume collision/passability rather than broad affordance or scene-state evolution.
VSI-Bench, Thinking in Space, MindCube, and related spatial-intelligence benchmarks are cited only for benchmark-design discipline and adjacent positioning, not for importing their QA categories.

findings.claim: The benchmark is unpublishable if public examples or labels remain template-authored rather than produced by the deterministic swept-cylinder oracle.
findings.evidence: input_manifest.json has data_manifest_path=null and data_manifest=null; blackboard.case_counts shows 50 needs_revision and 0 surviving cases.

findings.claim: The current phase gates overstate readiness.
findings.evidence: blackboard.phase_gates marks case_manifest_ready=true, but no data manifest is attached and reviewed_counts are 0 for every task.

findings.claim: The showcase requirements are necessary but not sufficient.
findings.evidence: The required fields include rgb_path, depth_path, topdown_path, sweep_overlay_path, visible_sweep_ratio, collision_point_visible, requires_hidden_geometry, fov_supported, bin_margin_body_widths, and oracle_trace_path; the visible cases only provide natural-language assumptions.

findings.claim: Most drafted cases could be solved or filtered without ego-body swept-volume reasoning.
findings.evidence: T1 can collapse to center-depth/bin priors; T2/T3 to largest visible floor patch or side preference; T4 to monotonic smaller-body priors; T5 to radius+horizon priors.

findings.claim: T4 has a serious action-confound risk.
findings.evidence: The prompt says each body moves the same number of its own body-widths, so changing radius changes both collision footprint and metric travel distance; this weakens the claimed do(body=r) isolation.

findings.claim: T3 and T5 should stay extension-only until visual evidence proves they do not require hidden-space inference.
findings.evidence: The goal explicitly excludes off-image, occluded, turn-corner, or hidden continuation labels; all current T3/T5 visibility fields are assumptions.

findings.claim: The case set covers the intended four skill layers only on paper, not as evidence.
findings.evidence: T1 covers metric measurement, T2 comparison, T3 action simulation, and T4 counterfactual reasoning by template labels, but no rendered scene demonstrates these distinctions.

findings.claim: The taxonomy is mostly grounded in goal.md, but paper wording should avoid looking like a copied general spatial-intelligence benchmark taxonomy.
findings.evidence: The blackboard names VSI-Bench, Thinking in Space, and MindCube as inspiration; public framing should retain EgoConseq's swept-volume readouts as the primary categories.

findings.claim: Freeze the benchmark design and route next to pipeline_verify, not more design debate.
findings.evidence: goal.md and benchmark_spec_v3 align on single-image, body-conditioned swept-volume consequence reasoning; case_generation_spec.status is frozen, but input_manifest.json has data_manifest_path=null and data_manifest=null.

findings.claim: Frozen showcase taxonomy is EgoConseq-derived: T1/T2/T4 are core demo families; T3/T5 are extension families.
findings.evidence: goal.md prioritizes T1/T2/T4 for the demo and defines T3/T5 as additional readouts of the same swept-volume formula; benchmark_spec_v3 marks T1/T2/T4 core and T3/T5 extension.

findings.claim: The final showcase must cite VSI-Bench, Thinking in Space, and MindCube only as methodology inspiration, not as copied task taxonomy.
findings.evidence: The frozen taxonomy is forward swept extent, directional sweep comparison, short composite action consequence, body intervention, and visible fixed-horizon passability, all derived from Body x Action_trajectory intersecting visible scene geometry.

findings.claim: No current illustrative case should be marked show in the HTML case showcase.
findings.evidence: All 50 visible case_author cases use assumed visibility language and lack rgb_path, depth_path, topdown_path, sweep_overlay_path, oracle_trace_path, non-null labels, margins, visible_sweep_ratio, fov_supported, and requires_hidden_geometry values.

findings.claim: All current case answers, visibility statements, rationales, H1/H2/H3 empirical claims, and validity-gate claims must be marked not simulator-validated.
findings.evidence: No M1/M2b/M4/M5/human results or simulator-backed data_manifest are present.

findings.claim: The blackboard phase gates overstate readiness.
findings.evidence: blackboard/state.json reports probe_verified=true and case_manifest_ready=true while input_manifest.json reports data_manifest_path=null and data_manifest=null.

recommendations: Minimal continue gate: at least 60 simulator-backed cases, with T1/T2/T4 each >=15 usable cases, all passing visibility/ambiguity filters and audit visualizations.

Require M4 oracle >=95%, blind M5 within about 5 percentage points of task chance/majority, human accuracy clearly above best VLM, and an oracle gap of at least about 20 percentage points on core tasks.
For H3, require same-image counterfactual groups where answer flips under body radius and where no-flip controls prevent the always-smaller shortcut; score pair consistency separately.
Freeze T1 bin thresholds only after the survey histogram; discard bin margins below 0.5 body-width.
Revise T4 so the counterfactual holds the action endpoint/horizon fixed in metric scene space, or explicitly separate collision-radius effects from body-normalized travel-distance effects.
Select showcase cases only when center-ray and largest-floor-patch heuristics fail on a meaningful subset; otherwise the demo does not isolate swept-volume reasoning.
Do not claim benchmark validity from the current 50 cases. Treat them as template coverage placeholders until replaced by data_manifest cases.
Adjudication decision: needs_pipeline_verify. The design_doc and case_generation_spec are frozen enough to execute the simulator/data pipeline.
Next artifact: produce data_manifest.json with at least 20 T1, 20 T2, and 20 T4 simulator-backed core cases; add T3/T5 only after visibility gates pass.
Each generated case must include RGB, depth, top-down, sweep overlay, oracle trace, label, max_safe_distance_body_widths, visibility metrics, margins, ambiguity fields, and counterfactual IDs.

Produce the two HTML deliverables only after the manifest exists: goal_taxonomy_cases.html with 10 reviewed cases per task, and design_rationale_capabilities.html explaining the taxonomy, validity gates, and novelty boundary.
Correct readiness bookkeeping: case_manifest_ready, probe_verified, and showcase_ready should remain false until real manifest/probe evidence is attached.
Keep all current 50 case_author items as template seeds only; do not use their answers for scoring or public validation claims.
